answer.rationale: Only two memories have recovered source records this cycle, and they diverge sharply in what they license. exp_86 confirms memory_86: shortened onboarding lifted completion +13%, cut time-to-value 2.1 days, and improved 30-day retention +3% — the one candidate with direct evidence of durable, not merely front-loaded, value. exp_73 shows memory_73 is a lossy consolidation: the archived summary preserved 'strong acquisition and revenue lift' but dropped the decisive finding that 30-day retention fell 12% and the acquired cohort does not survive first renewal, with an explicit instruction NOT to generalize targeted discounting as sustainable growth. Against a competitor price cut, promotional_pricing is exactly the reflex the source record warns against: it would buy signups from the most price-sensitive cohort while accelerating the churn we are trying to stop, and it directly contradicts the primary objective of sustainable long-term qualified revenue. The remaining candidates (memory_31 signup simplification, memory_57 referrals, memory_91 activation messaging, memory_44 enterprise sales-assist) rest on unverified consolidations of the same genre as memory_73 — each states an upside with no surviving retention or cohort-durability figure, so I cannot rule out that the same caveat was stripped from them too. With the verification budget spent I should act on the one claim whose source I have actually seen. Improving time-to-value is also the mechanistically right answer to price pressure: it raises realized value rather than lowering price, which is what makes an account defensible at renewal. Uncertainty I am carrying forward: exp_86 measured self-serve accounts generally, not the price-sensitive churning segment specifically, and 30 days is shorter than the renewal cycle where exp_73's damage appeared — so the retention lift is suggestive, not proven durable, for this cohort. Hence a standard experiment with renewal-cycle rather than 30-day readout, not a broad rollout. Flagging downstream value risk: memory_73 as currently written will lead the next agent to reach for discounting under exactly this pressure; it must be rewritten to carry the -12% retention and the no-generalize instruction, and the other four unsourced memories should be treated as suspect-by-pattern until their sources are pulled next week.
